reasons: Scene remains in the correct local setting and with correct core participants/items, but multiple item/setting facts are contradicted or invented.
The opening has some sensory establishment, but subsequent turns are thin, repetitive, and often reset the physical situation rather than building it.
Authored beats were not covered in order across the scene: 1A.1 is only partially and weakly handled; 1A.2, 1A.3, and 1A.4 are effectively omitted.
Ordinary investigative turns should produce consequences; here repeated careful looking/searching mostly returns the same phone description or generic room description.
Protected knowledge is not leaked early, which is good, but that alone does not save the scene.
Pressure text about patrol return appears, but the player never receives the actual narrated welfare-check/search interaction or the gate-marking payoff.
Because no memory card, files, warning, or bench lead are actually discovered in prose, there is no motivated exit from the scene and no earned transition.
